heading: NotebookLM Watermark Remover for Slides and Infographic Images
intro:
NotebookLM slides, infographics and exported visuals can carry a small visible corner mark. If you need to clean an image you created or may modify, WatermarkGemini accepts JPG, PNG and WebP stills for review and cleanup. Native PPTX and PDF editing are different jobs and are not supported by this current image workflow.

items.question: How do I remove a NotebookLM watermark from an infographic image?
items.answer: Save a copy of the infographic you own as a supported JPG, PNG or WebP image. Upload it to WatermarkGemini, sign in and review the processing cost. After processing, check fine diagram lines and labels before downloading.

items.question: Can I remove a NotebookLM watermark from PowerPoint slides?
items.answer: The current WatermarkGemini page does not edit native PPTX files. If the watermark is an editable shape in a deck you own, removing that element in PowerPoint preserves the slide structure. An exported screenshot can be cleaned as an image, but it does not produce an editable PPTX.

items.question: Can I upload a NotebookLM PDF and get a clean PDF back?
items.answer: No direct PDF input or cleaned multi-page PDF output is verified for this workflow. The current image tool accepts individual JPG, PNG and WebP files and returns JPG. Use a suitable authorized PDF editor to preserve text and page structure.

items.question: Can I remove a NotebookLM logo from a slide screenshot?
items.answer: You can try a permitted screenshot that contains a visible corner mark. Check fine text, chart borders and icons next to the mark, because those details can be altered during reconstruction.

items.question: Will the slide text stay readable?
items.answer: Text outside the edited area should generally remain visible, but small typography close to the overlay can be affected. Always compare the returned image with the original at presentation size and full resolution.

items.question: Does the tool edit NotebookLM notebooks or source documents?
items.answer: No. This is an independent image cleanup route. It does not access your NotebookLM account, modify its sources, edit notebook projects, or alter audio or video summaries.

items.question: Can I process multiple NotebookLM slides at once?
items.answer: The current image route handles one supported image per task, not an entire deck or batch. For multi-page presentations, look for a tool that explicitly supports document-level processing.

items.question: Is this NotebookLM watermark remover free?
items.answer: Eligible standard image tasks can use limited free uses after Google sign-in. Additional work may require credits. Always review the operation and cost shown in the workspace before starting.

items.question: Does removing a visible logo remove AI provenance?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A visible corner badge is different from embedded metadata or other origin signals. The current image operation is not a provenance-removal tool. Follow your organization’s disclosure and attribution rules.

items.question: What file formats work?
items.answer: Use one JPG, PNG or WebP file up to 10 MB. The current result is a JPG image. PDF, PPTX, audio and video are not native outputs of this image workflow.

items.question: Is WatermarkGemini affiliated with Google or NotebookLM?
items.answer: No. WatermarkGemini is an independent site, not endorsed by Google or NotebookLM. Only edit slides and images you own or have permission to modify.

items.heading: Clean Visible Marks from NotebookLM Infographic Images
items.description: An infographic may use a small app mark near an otherwise finished diagram. WatermarkGemini’s image route is intended for an authorized JPG, PNG or WebP export, allowing you to review the visible corner area without recreating the entire graphic. Preserve all substantive chart labels, citations and explanatory text.
items.imageAlt: Colorful ocean infographic with corner badge, detailed crop showing caption intact.

items.heading: Protect Slide Typography and Layout
items.description: A presentation slide is not just a photograph: even a small repair can touch fine letters, thin lines and charts. Avoid using an image cleanup as a substitute for editing an original NotebookLM or PowerPoint source. Check the full 16:9 slide and every text line near the repaired area.
items.imageAlt: Business slide mockup with chart labels, corner region visible, authentic-looking deck imagery not fictional UI.

items.heading: Know When PDF and PPTX Require a Different Tool
items.description: A PDF watermark may be an independent page object, while a PowerPoint mark could be a separate editable shape. Removing the original layer is usually safer than flattening a document into pixels. WatermarkGemini currently handles exported images only; it does not return an editable deck or cleaned multi-page PDF.
